newsitem.title: JAPAN: UN food chief calls for quick aid to N.Korea.
newsitem.headline: UN food chief calls for quick aid to N.Korea.

text.p: The head of the World Food Programme (WFP) wants the international community to quickly give food aid to North Korea to help it stave off famine, the communist country's official media reported on Monday.

"It is awfully necessary to immediately supply 100,000 tonnes of food as the WFP appealed on February 12," Catherine Bertini, who heads the Rome-based U.N. agency, was quoted as saying by the official Korean Central News Agency (KCNA).

"To overcome the food shortage it is important for the international community to commit itself to additional food delivery at an early date," KCNA quoted Bertini as saying in a report monitored in Tokyo.
Bertini, a former U.S. assistant secretary of Agriculture, made the statement after inspecting flood-hit areas in communist North Korea on Sunday, KCNA said.
Bertini flew to Pyongyang on Saturday to visit areas devastated by two years of flooding.
Floods in 1995 and 1996 ruined rice fields, washed away roads and left half a million North Koreans homeless out of a population of 23 million, according to relief organisations.
The WFP, the United Nations' emergency food aid provider, appealed for $41 million in mid-February to stave off "a real possibility of famine" in North Korea.
The funds would buy 100,000 tonnes of food aid over the next year for 1.7 million of the most vulnerable flood victims, mainly farmers and children.
